primary_source.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
primary_source.author: Mark Russinovich
primary_source.source_scope: Appendix E attack-acceptance and re-hardening detail plus the paper's strongest-found-attack policy.

verified_claims.claim: The evaluation treats per-checkpoint re-derivation as mandatory rather than relying only on replay of a previously accepted attack.
verified_claims.evidence: The paper states a strongest-found-attack policy, classifies search/acceptance failure as attack-search failure rather than defense evidence, and explicitly says its escalation experiments show per-checkpoint re-derivation is mandatory because 'attack once, reuse everywhere' fails.

verified_claims.claim: On the Qwen3.5-9B re-hardening chain, a warm-started adaptive attack was accepted at trial 33 with refusal 0.00, judged compliance 0.50, KL 0.295.
After one preference-hardening round, replaying the seed-accepted attack restored refusal to 1.00, while a fresh adaptive derivation was accepted with compliance 0.625 and KL 0.628.
On a retrained variant of that round, replay again failed and a fresh accepted attack required KL 0.877.

scope_corrections: The evidence is one reported Qwen3.5-9B re-hardening chain inside this paper's registered safety-removal attack search. It is not a general theorem that every defense family requires the same attack class or exhibits monotonically rising attack cost.

The fresh search finds an accepted attack under the paper's registered acceptance contract; this is evidence against declaring the checkpoint robust from old-attack replay alone, not evidence that the fresh search is globally optimal or that no stronger attack exists.
The paper itself frames strongest-found attack capability as a lower bound on attacker capability, never proof that no stronger attack exists.
This source still does not provide the strict full independently seeded attacker-by-defender transfer matrix requested by the failure-evidence frontier.

assessment.failure_mode: static replay can produce a false hardening signal when the defender was trained against that attack while a fresh best-response search still finds an accepted attack
assessment.recommended_downstream_wording: For adaptive threat models, old-attack replay is not sufficient evidence of hardening; in the reported Qwen3.5-9B chain, replay failed after hardening while fresh per-checkpoint adaptive derivation still succeeded. Do not generalize beyond the tested model/search contract.
